experiences.text: Use PRA-MAINT rather than PRA-MAINTAINABILITY for duplication and drift findings; the long-form label correlates with lower-reward reviews.
Prioritize identifying critical runtime errors such as division by zero in weighted average calculations.

Verify the 'supply chain cleared' claim is enforceable: the PR-Agent 0.44.0 pin/lockfile must be committed in the tagged release and the pip-audit clean result must cite the exact resolution tree and scan time, otherwise state in the changelog that the audit is unpinned and can drift.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Use the repo's PRA-SEC type instead of PRA-SECURITY; the verbose variant reads as a duplicate of already-reported secret-injection findings and gets dismissed.
Replace hardcoded indentation constants in CommonMark rendering with dynamic calculation to prevent future regressions.

Lead with concrete, verifiable config-semantics conflicts — e.g., whether `kind: suppress` on PRA-POSSIBLE_ISSUE contradicts the '只压子集' comment by hiding the 5 adopted real bugs, whether ERR-002's over_engineering category collides with OE-001, and whether renumbered Pattern ordinals break hardcoded references (grep before asserting).

Frame review notes as concrete one-line fixes humans can apply immediately — correct the stale '样本 20/20' footnote to '20/20/10', delimit ERR-002's 外部边界 against ERR-001, and name the source-of-truth file for the thrice-duplicated ERR-002 text.
Do not suggest rounding counts to '约 1200' as a maintainability fix; the actionable ask is CI generation, and approximation reads as dodging the measurement problem.

Drop the threat-model framing that anyone with variables write access can silently bypass the gate — reviewers dismiss it as overwrought for an internal threshold; put the auditability ask inside PRA-RISK instead.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Drop the changelog-provenance nit about '（用户指示）' — all four reviewers repeated it and humans dismiss wording-only objections to unreleased changelog phrasing.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

Identify where a mock or explicit env flag sidesteps the very behavior an audit item claims to fix (pagination aggregation, default-off retirement) and specify the exact missing companion or negative test to add.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Skip abstract robustness musings about invariants; when keep-last marker fragility matters, file it as a PRA-BUG with a failing input, not a 'consider anchoring' note.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.
Consolidate release-verification claims fragmented across PRA-TEST/PRA-RELEASE/PRA-RELEASE-DATE/PRA-RELEASE-CONSISTENCY into one PRA-PROCESS finding instead of emitting near-duplicates.
Avoid leaving speculative review comments that ask developers to confirm assumptions, verify implementation details, or expand scope without identifying a concrete bug.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.
Ensure API error handling fails explicitly rather than returning empty strings to prevent false negatives in security scans.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.

Call out the internal contradiction in atomicio.py where os.fchmod is Windows-guarded but _fsync_dir immediately opens a directory fd that Windows does not support, so atomic_write_text still fails on Windows despite the stated portability goal.
Omit 'historical comments remain corrupt' caveats and doc-note suggestions on hotfixes; reviewers treat pre-existing-data commentary as out of scope.
Do not report potential TypeErrors from deserializing legacy JSON markers when fields are removed from state dataclasses.
Verify that the remaining items provide sufficient coverage for essential review dimensions after the cleanup.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.

Do not pad PRA-DESIGN with restatements of the hallucination-versus-negative-reward argument, jq arithmetic checks, or future-timestamp forensics — fold pipeline fixes into PRA-ROBUSTNESS and reversibility into PRA-PREVENT instead.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.

Sweep stale narration to the link-only contract — the '恒出现——不依赖受评仓是否携带 skills/' docstring framing, SKILL.md §0/§4 copy-drift discussion, and README/changelog mentions of the二级折叠 — because docs describing deleted behavior cause the next reader to restore it.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress suggestions to make anti-drift tests robust against the specific structural variations they are designed to detect and prevent.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Skip minor formatting nits such as duplicated parentheticals or blockquote placement on release PRs, where reviewers act only on substantive release-integrity checks.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Ignore findings flagging future-dated comments in snapshot files as these are likely intentional simulation placeholders.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Avoid hedged 'diff looks truncated, verify the implementation exists' completeness complaints; fold any real risk into a concrete PRA-BUG instead.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.

Avoid speculative doc findings on version-bump PRs (confirm PR #214 is merged, sweep hypothetical pinning docs for stale version references) unless you can cite an actual stale file — unverifiable 'confirm/sweep' doc asks get ignored on release commits.
Drop unclosed-file-handle and local-import nitpicks on one-line test reads; humans ignore resource-hygiene complaints in test code.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.
Suppress speculative design generalizations such as extending the GitCode denylist to Gitee/Gitea absent evidence those forges are in scope.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Identify and flag obvious factual errors such as incorrect dates or contradictory information.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.

Consolidate test findings into one concrete note (monkeypatch os.path.exists/builtins.open to raise to enforce '渲染零文件依赖', extract the copy-pasted <details> splitter shared by both tests, replace the magic len(frag)<500) instead of scattering them across invented labels.

Don't restate the semver complaint under PRA-VERSIONING, PRA-COMPAT-SEMVER, or PRA-CONTRACT-DOC variants; one decisive PRA-COMPAT finding covering both the version question and schema-drift check is what gets acted on.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.

Verify deeply, not generically: check the runner's unset-vs-empty-string fallback semantics, whether 128000 is provider-dependent, and that quoted comments match source verbatim (reviewers caught CHANGELOG.md's shortened 「宁可看全 diff」 quote diverging from the code).

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.

Anchor design comments to the recorded #192 decision with exactly one actionable suggestion (e.g., inline the one-line ack format spec so offline agents keep it) rather than open-ended tradeoff essays.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.

Propose a CI consistency check asserting __version__ == pyproject version == newest CHANGELOG heading — only the top review surfaced it and it directly targets this repo's declared version-drift failure mode.

Run concrete greps: hunt leftover hardcoded 0.3.5 strings (tests, README, SECURITY.md, badges), confirm pyproject's dynamic attr resolves 0.3.6 on a build, and check the changelog's env names match the strings the code actually reads.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.
Drop speculative PRA-RISK musings about hypothetical infrastructure failures unless tied to a concrete misconfiguration actually visible in the diff.
Stop demanding audit evidence (CI runs, #216 diffs) for the 'zero behavior change' claim — the best-received review simply accepted the explicit parity note.
Omit post-merge release mechanics advice about tag naming and publish-workflow triggers — it lives outside the diff and gets dismissed.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.

Do not demand a 0.4.0 minor bump for feature entries — 0.x feature-as-patch is a project convention choice, this critique appears only in low-reward reviews, and the top review accepted the patch bump.
Drop wording audits of '契约零变化'-style claims that hinge on zero-change vs no-breaking-change distinctions; humans treat these as semantic quibbles on a release-only diff and ignore them.

Verify the hardcoded 2026-09-10 date, grep for stale 0.3.6 references (SECURITY.md 支持范围, README badges, install docs), run a CLI --version smoke check on the dynamic pyproject read, and assign an owner for post-merge tag/GitHub-release steps.
Require inline rationale comments to be rewritten whenever the value they justify changes, so stale 'small model is enough, latency halved' arguments stop contradicting new defaults.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Do not demand companion tests for adjacent branches (missing skill path, packaging validation of the deployed SKILL.md) when the PR's stated goal is just making the existing regression test hermetic — scope-expanding coverage asks were penalized.

Lead with the verifiable mismatch between the commit message's '299 hallucinated finding_type' claim and deletions of canonical PRA-* entries carrying genuine tfgrpo provenance, demanding the real retention criterion plus a kept/removed ID manifest.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.

Do not demand repopulation plans or before/after review-quality comparisons when a data store shrinks — this repo has long-learned suppression of PRA-COVERAGE and both negative-reward reviews confirm it is dismissed again here.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

On release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus the version bump, raise the changelog-vs-diff artifact reconciliation once as a concrete verification action (confirm each advertised file actually landed via its linked PR before tagging).
Offer a light consistency nit suggesting the heading keep the minimal 'version — date' format with the summary carried in the body, matching prior entries like [0.3.5].
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
Flag a title/diff mismatch only when the title's explicit promise is verifiably absent from the diff (e.g. 「README 精简」with zero deletions), and supply the corrected title in the finding itself.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.

Flag concrete changelog-completeness gaps — the missing itemized entry for PR #218 (preflight 文案对齐), the heading that names only the visibility feature while the summary claims two PRs, and the review-process meta-narrative ('评审 3 轮收敛') that doesn't belong in user-facing release notes.

Suppress the 'release PR ships no code — verify #218/#222 are merged before tagging' boilerplate (and its PRA-RELEASE-SCOPE/PRA-RELEASE-PREREQ variants) — version+changelog-only diffs are inherent to release PRs, unverifiable from this diff, and the highest-reward review skipped it entirely.

Skip speculative heading re-parenting audits of the former unreleased section — only the lowest-reward review raised it and the visible diff shows no stray pending notes being silently attributed to 0.3.7.

Use the canonical finding types the top review uses (PRA-DOC, PRA-PROCESS, PRA-QUESTION) instead of one-off variant names (PRA-CHANGELOG-AUDIENCE/COMPLETENESS/COVERAGE, PRA-DATE-ACCURACY/DATE-VERIFY/RELEASE-DATE, PRA-LINKREF-MISSING, PRA-DOC-SYNC, PRA-STALE-VERSION-REFS, PRA-HEADING-SCOPE-MISMATCH, PRA-RELEASE-VERIFICATION) for identical findings — type fragmentation reads as noise.

Lead with the one decisive contradiction that the new 'AI Committer' title implies merge authority while the README's own first bullet says AI review is advisory-only (只给建议、不拦截合入) and the deterministic gate is what actually enforces merges.

Filter deleted-section findings down to genuinely operational facts — the LLM Secrets→Variables dual-read fallback, the `touchstone doctor` self-check entry, and the `TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR` isolation for concurrent PR reviews — and request a one-line relocation pointer to docs/DEPLOYMENT.md instead of opposing the simplification itself.
Omit PRA-PRAISE on simplification PRs — complimenting the author's own changelog discipline appeared only in a lowest-reward review and adds no actionable signal.
Replace hedged PRA-QUESTION findings such as 'is the AI-vs-AI tagline intentional?' with a single direct recommendation, since tentative questions about the tagline read as padding.
Keep doc-only deletions at MINOR-or-below rather than PRA-MAJOR — severity inflation on a deliberate slimming PR drew the lowest rewards.
Consolidate speculative dead-link sweeps (grep for the renamed H1 anchor, dangling 本地命令/规模与状态 section references) into one consistency finding instead of separate REFERENCE/VERIFY/NAMING entries.
Drop repo-wide "grep for stale phrasing" advice on docs-only PRs unless you actually ran the grep and can name the file and line that still carries the old wording.
Do not demand extra verbatim assertions in doc-drift tests for half-phrases or README strings; speculative coverage asks on synced documentation read as noise and get dismissed.
Skip requests that policy docs define terms like 『定向』 unless the undefined term would change what an agent actually executes; definitional quibbles on skill prose are ignored.
Never file comment-accuracy nitpicks whose own note concedes the value is correct (e.g. 700 vs the proportional 720) — reviewers dismiss these outright.
Suppress doc-clarity findings you would label 低优先级 yourself; a line already disambiguated by an adjacent cross-reference does not need rewriting.
Omit positive consistency confirmations entirely — praising aligned CHANGELOG/render/test wording spends review credibility without changing anything.
Treat silent default relaxations of hard gates (e.g. TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES 1000→3000) as policy changes and require an explicit upgrade note telling deployments how to pin the old strictness.

Demand proof within this PR's diff that every claimed sync of code defaults, warning text, and tests actually exists, because a comment describing a nonexistent fallback default is worse than no comment.
Make the quick-start enumerate every required secret and repo variable and keep touchstone doctor as an explicit preflight step before promising an X-minute deployment.

Verify every newly referenced model id (reflect glm-4.7, e2e fallback glm-5.3) actually resolves on the deployment and CI endpoints before merging, since an unverified id breaks improve or e2e for everyone.
Skip jargon-wording suggestions like defining internal terms such as 销项流程, since readers dismiss vocabulary nitpicks in a docs rewrite.
Skip speculative maturity critiques like TF-GRPO overselling unless the doc flatly contradicts implemented behavior.
Do not file generic 'the diff is truncated, please manually re-verify' items, as readers dismiss requests to redo the reviewer's own verification.

Verify what the diff cannot show: that the Keep-a-Changelog footer gained the [0.3.6] compare link and the [未发布] range moved to v0.3.6, and that tag/publish-workflow/SECURITY.md release mechanics are owned — the one finding every reviewer raised and the top-scoring review kept.

Include a positive note crediting what the release PR does well (the 未发布 placeholder convention preserved, the zero-behavior-change scoping clearly stated) — praise appears only in the top-scoring review.
Drop policy debates about whether a CI-config-only change deserves its own patch release — authors dismiss scope philosophizing on a release PR they already decided to cut.
Stop speculating about whether referenced PR #216 is already merged; the reviewer cannot verify another PR's merge state from this diff, so at most state the tagging precondition once.

Suppress restating the generic tag-push-publish playbook across multiple findings (tag v0.3.3, GitHub Release notes mirroring, artifact build) — one brief confirmation of the release step suffices and repetition reads as boilerplate.

Skip demands for linked CI-run evidence or secrets/vars namespace essays to back the zero-change claim; humans act on the checkable version (grep env names against code), not proof-of-verification requests.

Lead release-PR reviews with the version-gap rationale: demand a concrete, traceable reason for burning 0.3.4 and insist the note states whether any v0.3.4 tag or artifact exists, rather than accepting the circular 'skipped because unpublished'.
In Keep-a-Changelog files, always inspect the compare-link block at the bottom and require the [0.3.5]: v0.3.3...v0.3.5 entry plus a retargeted [未发布] link in the same PR.

Anchor stale-version checks in the repo's own single-source comment (__init__.py) and instruct a grep for hardcoded "0.3.3" across SECURITY.md, README badges, and version-asserting tests before merging the bump.

Require the changelog date (2026-09-02) to match the actual tag/publish day and convert the coincidence of version+changelog sharing one PR into the proposed CI check that changelog top version equals touchstone.__version__.
Treat user-facing claims like '判定/引擎/CLI 契约零变化' as needing evidence: verify PR #214 touched only docs/presentation files and ask for its file list to be attached to the release notes.
Drop the standalone version-skip finding that merely restates the rationale/artifact check and speculates about release scripts assuming '+1 increments' without any evidence such a script exists.
Do not file separate findings against untouched files like SECURITY.md when the same supported-range risk is already covered by the diff-grounded stale-version sweep.
Omit speculative downstream concerns such as monitoring consumers misalarmed by a missing 0.3.4 sequence point, which reviewers dismiss as outside this release PR's scope.
Avoid proposing changelog restructuring like a placeholder '## [0.3.4] — 已跳过' section; the blockquote note under 0.3.5 is the convention reviewers accept.

Emphasize the diff-grounded risk that inserting the '[0.3.3]' heading silently re-attributes everything still sitting under '[未发布]' to the release — audit each swept-in entry against what actually shipped since v0.3.2.
Suppress hedged conditionals like 'add a [0.3.3] link reference if the file uses Keep-a-Changelog, otherwise ignore' — inspect the file footer first or drop the finding.
Suppress formatting nits on a two-line release diff (em-dash separators, heading-format matching, duplicate issue mentions, placeholder wording) — humans dismiss them as noise.
Suppress proposing new CI checks or version-consistency tests inside a release-only changelog PR — keep suggestions scoped to what this diff actually changes.
Suppress low-risk date-confirmation nits on the hardcoded 2026-09-02 heading unless the release can realistically slip past it.
Suppress splitting the same claim-verification (PR #212 merged, tests exist, contract untouched) into several near-duplicate findings — verify once and report once.

Flag the additive unreviewed_files/unreviewed_total fields shipped in a patch bump (0.3.1→0.3.2) as an observable contract change for strict-schema consumers, demanding either a minor bump or a documented policy that additive JSON fields are patch-compatible.
Don't invent hyphenated subtypes like PRA-DOC-LINK for missing changelog reference definitions; fold them into a single canonical PRA-DOC item, which is what the top-rewarded review does.
Drop speculative structure-migration checklists asking whether bullets were 'swept under the new header' when nothing is actually wrong with the section placement.
Suppress stylistic opinions about heading verbosity, duplicated summaries, and whether hardcoded test counts 'invite staleness'; humans dismiss prose-preference nitpicks on release notes.
Avoid splitting supply-chain verification into a PRA-SUPPLYCHAIN subtype; keep it under PRA-SECURITY where reviewers engage with the pin/audit evidence.

Lead with a PRA-VERIFY proving the new env entry sits on the step/job that actually launches the code reading TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES (not the pr_agent_runner/LiteLLM step), citing the step's run command or this PR's own CI logs showing the resolved threshold.

Foreground the concrete crash path: Actions exports TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES='' (present-but-empty) when the repo variable is unset, so int('') raises unless orchestrator._max_diff_lines guards it as int(v) if v.strip() else 1000 — point to or add that guard.

Demand unit tests for the now-live parsing paths (unset, '', '0', valid number, garbage) plus a pre-merge end-to-end run setting the repo variable to a distinctive value like 10 to prove the SIZE-001 gate actually reacts.

Require the now-live operator semantics (unset/'' → default 1000, '0' → gate off) to land in README/vars docs and have the workflow comment reference the orchestrator source as the single source of truth to prevent drift.
Frame this fix as one instance of the documented-but-never-wired dead-config bug class and sweep sibling tunables like TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS in the same pass.
Raise one PRA-RISK that '0' silently disables the gate and ask that the effective threshold (plus an explicit gate-disabled notice) be logged every run so overrides are auditable.
Cover malformed values ('1,000', trailing spaces, 'abc') under PRA-ROBUSTNESS by requesting warn-and-fallback-to-default parsing instead of a distant ValueError crash mid-run.
Offer mechanical polish (quoting "${{ vars.TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES }}", matching block alignment) as a single explicitly deferrable PRA-NIT rather than standalone findings.
Do not file input-validation as PRA-VALIDATION; fold malformed-value handling into PRA-BUGRISK/PRA-ROBUSTNESS notes where it actually gets acted on.
Avoid PRA-COMPLETE checklists about other jobs, reusable workflows, and env forwarding; the missing-coverage sweep belongs in one PRA-SWEEP note.
Never mint hyphenated PRA-VERIFY-* subtypes — the consumer-side empty-string check is a standard PRA-VERIFY/PRA-BUGRISK note.
Fold step/job plumbing confirmation into the single canonical PRA-VERIFY instead of a custom PRA-VERIFY-PLUMBING type.
Do not invent PRA-RISK-BEHAVIOR-CHANGE for dead-config activation; if the currently-set variable value matters, state it in one line inside PRA-RISK.
Skip PRA-RISK-SEMANTICS essays on '0'-counterintuition and token-budget coupling; fold the warning-log ask into PRA-RISK and the documentation into PRA-DOC.
Suppress PRA-PROCESS meta-advice (startup logging mandates, org-wide audits); convert it into the concrete PRA-SWEEP and PRA-TEST asks reviewers accept.
Drop PRA-STYLE-NIT dual-source-of-truth musings; the single-source-of-truth point belongs in PRA-DOC and cosmetic nits stay in PRA-NIT.

Lead with breaking contract changes and fail-open logic: enumerate every caller of a changed signature (e.g., get_diff_from_git now returning a (diff, any_ok) tuple) and the exact silent misjudgment each missed caller would make.

Flag concrete CI breakage with the one-line fix: pip installs piped through tail without pipefail, referenced-but-uncommitted files like pragent-constraints.txt, and stub JSON that makes 'skipped' indistinguishable from 'zero findings'.

Call out duplicated pins and configs across .gitcode and .github workflows (e.g., PRA_VERSION=0.39.0 written twice under a 'same caliber' comment) as a live drift source and demand a single source of truth or consistency check.

Report secrets injected before the event gate and hardcoded repo fallbacks (CI_REPO_OWNER/CI_REPO_NAME :-defaults) as concrete structural fixes: conditional step, inject after gating, fail hard on missing context variables.

Audit sibling tests in the touched module for residual reads of the deployed skills/ directory in the same pass, since partially hermeticizing one test leaves the stated #192 motivation (dev checkouts without skills/) still red.
Do not invent a PRA-CI label for workflow findings; fold them into PRA-OPS or PRA-BUG, the types reviewers actually act on in this repo.
